claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The baseline alloy was produced from high-purity elemental powders by ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a low-temperature yield strength of about 800 MPa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
About 1 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles should be incorporated into the TiVNbTa powder before ball milling and SPS consolidation.
The added Y2O3 nanoparticles will form a uniform nanoscale dispersion.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will provide pinning points at grain boundaries and within grains.
Nanoparticle pinning will stabilize the BCC matrix against high-temperature grain coarsening.
The oxide dispersion will reduce dislocation mobility at elevated temperature.
Y2O3 particles will obstruct dislocation glide and recovery processes at high temperature.
Y2O3 particle pinning will delay grain-boundary sliding.
Y2O3 particle pinning will delay dynamic recrystallization.
Suppressing recovery, grain-boundary sliding, and dynamic recrystallization will reduce thermally activated softening and retain higher strength.
The Y2O3-strengthened alloy will exceed the 330 MPa baseline yield strength at 1273 K by an amount on the order of tens of MPa.
The strengthened alloy will retain adequate ductility for use as a thermal-transfer layer.
The intervention is intended for service near 1273 K under tensile or compressive loading comparable to the baseline test conditions.
A similar SPS schedule may use a sintering temperature of approximately 1543 K.
The proposal assumes that adding 1 vol% Y2O3 will not adversely affect the thermal diffusivity needed between W and CuCrZr.
Oxide-dispersion strengthening is established in other high-temperature alloys.
The strength improvement may depend on nanoparticle dispersion quality and particle-matrix interface characteristics.
